questions.question: What is the durability test that decides whether a piece of information belongs in repo memory?
options: Whether it is JSON
Whether it would be useful three months from now in a CI rerun; if yes, repo; if no, telemetry
Whether the user marked it as important
Whether it fits in 4 kB
questions.explanation: Repo memory is for durable, three-months-from-now-useful state; transient data is telemetry.

questions.question: What schema field carries the agent's contract version?
options: schema_version
build_hash
model_id
session_uuid
questions.explanation: schema_version is the integer contract; the manager refuses to load from an unknown version.

questions.question: How does atomic write work?
options: tempfile.mkstemp in the same directory, write, fsync, os.replace (atomic rename) over the target
Truncate-then-write to the target
Append-only with a CRC
Encrypt and overwrite
questions.explanation: Atomic rename on POSIX and Windows is what prevents partial-write corruption.

questions.question: Per the lesson's repo-memory table, which of these does NOT belong in repo memory?
options: The active task id, tracked so the next session knows where to resume
Raw chat transcripts, which stay in the conversation, not the repo
Any open blockers, tracked so nobody re-discovers a known problem
The next action, tracked so the next session has a concrete start
questions.explanation: The lesson's table lists raw chat transcripts under 'Does not belong'; active task id, open blockers, and next action all belong in repo memory.

questions.question: What does the lesson say schema-first state buys you?
options: It lets the agent skip validation once the schema has been defined once
It compresses the state file so checkpoints load faster across sessions
Without a schema, agents invent fields; with one, bad writes are refused
It replaces atomic writes, since the schema already guarantees durability
questions.explanation: The lesson says: without a schema, every agent invents new fields, every reviewer learns a new shape, and every CI script has to special-case past versions; with it, a bad write is a refused write.

questions.question: What four things does the schema constrain, per the lesson?
options: File size limits, text encoding, line endings, and commit message format
The model provider, token budget, temperature, and system prompt used
Branch name, commit author, timestamp format, and total diff size
Required keys, allowed statuses, forbidden values, and pattern rules
questions.explanation: The lesson lists what the schema covers: required keys, allowed status values, forbidden values (e.g. null for arrays), and pattern constraints (task ids match T-\d{3,}).

questions.question: What does the lesson say happens when schema_version mismatches?
options: The manager silently upgrades
The manager refuses to load until a migration script in tools/migrate_state.py runs
The state is deleted
The agent retries
questions.explanation: Schema migrations or refuse-to-load; never silent upgrade.
